# QS-CFW-1159-60 — Quality specification - track link CFW-1159-60 (15B37)
Revision: Rev F  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-1159-60  
This revision supersedes Rev E.

Scope
- This quality specification applies to forged track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) produced at Plant P3. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and handling of nonconforming material for production, heat treatment, machining, and final inspection operations associated with the part family identified above. The scope includes forged blanks, finished machined links, and assembled link sets delivered under the CFW-1159-60 part identifier.

Background and rationale
- Track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is a high-wear component used in undercarriage systems. The functional life of the component depends on controlled hardness, accurate bore geometry, and adherence to forging weight limits to ensure proper material flow during forming and consistent heat treatment response. The hardness range is set to balance wear resistance with fracture toughness for application conditions. Bore tolerance controls press-fit and pin retention; the specified forging weight limit ensures die life and consistent microstructure in the finished part. These parameters were selected based on historical production data and laboratory correlation of hardness to fatigue performance.

Requirements table
- Material and identification
  - Material shall be as specified on the purchase order for parts CFW-1159-60. Each delivered part shall be legibly marked or tagged with the part identifier CFW-1159-60 and the heat lot or batch code associated with the melt.

- Hardness
  - The hardness range for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 36-40 HRC.

- Bore diameter
  - The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is ±0.01 mm.

- Forging weight
  - The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 80.0 kg.

- Surface condition and discontinuities
  - Forgings shall be free of visible forging laps, through-thickness cracks, and other discontinuities that would compromise service performance. Light mill scale and minor surface oxide permitted if removed prior to final inspection.

- Documentation and traceability
  - Each batch shall be accompanied by manufacturing records showing heat lot, forging operation reference, heat-treatment record, and final inspection sign-off.

Inspection method
- Overview
  - Inspections are performed at incoming material receipt, post-forging, post-heat-treatment, post-machining, and final inspection before shipment. Critical characteristics listed in the requirements table shall be verified by qualified personnel using calibrated equipment traceable to internal calibration records.

- Hardness measurement procedure
  - Perform hardness readings on the machined or heat-treated surface at locations representative of the high-wear regions and the web near the bore. Use an appropriate Rockwell hardness tester calibrated per internal calibration practice. Take multiple readings across the component to account for local variation. Record individual readings and calculate the observed range. Parts outside the stated hardness range shall be identified as nonconforming.

- Bore diameter measurement procedure
  - Inspect bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or coordinate measuring equipment capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Measure at several axial positions and at orthogonal angles to detect out-of-round conditions. Record nominal values and deviations. Accept only those parts where all measured bore diameters fall within the tolerance band defined in the requirements table.

- Forging weight verification
  - Verify forging weight at the forging operation by weighing the blank after trimming and prior to heat treatment. Ensure each blank does not exceed the maximum forging weight specified in the requirements table. Record the measured weight on the forging route card.

- Sampling and frequency
  - Selectivity for sampling shall be aligned with process capability and risk assessment. For routine production, include hardness and bore checks on every lot prior to machining and on finished parts. For low-volume or prototype runs, increase inspection coverage as required by engineering.

- Calibration and equipment
  - Use calibrated instruments for hardness, dimensional, and mass measurements. Record calibration references and due dates in the inspection record.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any part or lot found outside the specified requirements shall be tagged as nonconforming and segregated from conforming stock. Marking shall include part identifier, lot code, and the nature of the nonconformance.

- Evaluation and disposition
  - Engineering shall evaluate nonconforming items to determine root cause and disposition. Disposition options include rework, repair, use-as-is with concession, or scrap. For hardness out-of-specification items, evaluate potential reheat or reprocessing only after metallurgical assessment confirms rework will restore required properties without introducing detrimental effects. For bore tolerance issues, evaluate whether machining corrections are feasible without impacting part geometry or function.

- Example dispositions
  - Example: A lot exhibiting hardness below the specified range may be held for microstructural analysis; if analysis shows incomplete transformation, reheat and controlled quench may be authorized by engineering with documented parameters and subsequent verification to the hardness criteria. Example: A bore slightly oversize beyond tolerance may be rejected for service use and either scrapped or returned to vendor if outside repair capability.

- Root cause and corrective action
  - Initiate formal corrective action when nonconformance indicates process drift or recurring defects. Document root cause, containment actions, corrective actions, and verify effectiveness through follow-up inspections and trend data.

Records to keep
- Maintain the following records with the lot history for each production batch of CFW-1159-60:
  - Forging route card with measured forging weight and operator sign-off.
  - Heat-treatment records tied to the heat lot.
  - Hardness test records showing individual readings and location notation.
  - Dimensional inspection reports including bore measurements and instrument identification.
  - Nonconformance reports and disposition documentation.
  - Final inspection sign-off and packing release.

Retention
- Inspection and traceability records shall be retained in the document control system per Plant P3 record retention practice and made available for customer review upon request.

Notes
- This specification is the controlling quality requirement for CFW-1159-60 at Plant P3. Any deviation from the requirements above must be authorized in writing by engineering and documented on the lot record prior to shipment.
